L141: Owners and 【46†referring vets】 seeking to enroll an animal in a current study should carefully review the study description and enrollment criteria below.
L142: ### Need more options?

L147: ## Current clinical trials and translational research studies at VMCVM

L150: 
L151: 【48†Image: horse photo】
L152: 
L153: 【22†Evaluation of a treatment for Equine Osteoarthritis】
L154: 
L155: The purpose of this study is to assess the effect of BIO-PLY on lameness reduction in horses affected with osteoarthritis.
L156: 
L157:     * 【49†tag: Horses】
L158:     * 【50†tag: Recruiting】

L162: 【51†Image: horse photo】
L163: 
L164: 【23†A study of Paroxetine in Horses】
L165: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the pharmacokinetics and clinical efficacy of paroxetine, a human antidepressant, in horses after single and 30-day doses. By finding a safe and effective dosage, this research aims to improve management and quality of life for horses displaying stereotypic behaviors like cribbing, wind sucking, and weaving
L166:

L170: 
L171: 【24†Non-invasive treatment of Equine melanomas】
L172: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the effectiveness of using histotripsy, a non-invasive treatment, to treat melanomas in horses and measure its impact on the immune system.

L182: 【25†A Non-Invasive Approach to treating Equine Sarcoids】
L183: Purpose: To evaluate the effectiveness of histotripsy as a non-invasive therapeutic approach for treating equine sarcoids.

L190: 【56†Image: Dog photo 】
L191: 
L192: 【26†Liver tumor PDT】
L193: The purpose of this study is to test a new treatment called photodynamic therapy (PDT) for dogs who've been diagnosed with liver tumors. The goal is to find out if PDT can be done safely, and see if it helps destroy the tumor cells in the liver. The long term objective is to develop a minimally invasive way of treating liver tumors.

L201: 【58†Image: Dog photo for thyroid tumors】
L202: 【27†Developing a non-invasive treatment for canine thyroid tumors】
L203: 
L204: The purpose of the study is to evaluate histotripsy, a new, non-invasive way of treating canine thyroid tumors that can precisely target and destroy abnormal tissues without incisions or radiation.
L205:

L212: 【59†Image: PlN study dog photo】
L213: 
L214: 【28†Evaluating a Clotting Enzyme in Dogs with Protein Losing Nephropathy】
L215: The purpose of the study is to evaluate a clotting enzyme, ADAMTS13, in dogs with protein losing nephropathy (PLN). Protein losing nephropathy is a form of kidney disease that causes protein loss in the urine. Dogs with PLN have a higher risk of blood clotting disorders, but the mechanism isn’t well understood.

L225: 【29†Comparing measurements in dogs with Pulmonary Hypertension】
L226: The purpose of this study is to compare the accuracy of measurements in the lungs obtained from a non-invasive heart ultrasound (echocardiogram) to the measurements obtained from right heart catheterization to better diagnose, classify, and treat pulmonary hypertension in dogs.

L237: Purpose: To determine if it is safe and feasible to use a light-sensitive drug called verteporfin, in combination with photodynamic therapy (PDT), in dogs with newly diagnosed brain tumors.

L259: 【32†Amputation and Chemotherapy for Osteosarcoma】
L260: We are seeking dogs whose owners have decided on the standard of care treatment option for canine osteosarcoma. This includes amputation and chemotherapy. This study aims to check for the spread (metastasis) of the cancer and will follow patients until the time which the dog develops metastasis. We will use this information to compare against our other clinical trials.
